LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 12.2 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY:

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.1: Listening and Speaking 12.2 Pronunciation and Vocabulary:
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 12.2 Pronunciation and Vocabulary:, part of Strand 12 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we speak clearly and confidently? 2. Why do we make speeches?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. say words containing the sounds /f/ and /v/ with peers,

2. pronounce the words related to the theme correctly,

3. construct oral sentences using vocabulary learnt, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. say words containing the sounds /f/ and /v/ with peers,
2. pronounce the words related to the theme correctly,
3. construct oral sentences using vocabulary learnt, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 12.2 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Collaboration is achieved as the learner works with peers to say minimal pairs of sounds /f/ and /v/.

• Self-efficacy is achieved as the learner creates and makes short speeches using appropriate non-verbal cues.

Values:
Patriotism is cultivated as the learner listens to a recorded speech from a digital device on environmental pollution.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental Education is promoted as learners interact with content related to environmental pollution while they

listen to the recorded speech.
